newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says U.S. impedes arrival of food, medicines.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says U.S. impedes arrival of food, medicines.

text.p: Iraq said on Sunday the United States was impeding the arrival of food and medicine supplies under an oil-for-food deal signed with the United Nations.

"Food and medicine have not yet arrived to the Iraqi people because of complications which are put by America in the (U.N.) sanctions committee," said Baghdad radio, reporting a cabinet meeting chaired by President Saddam Hussein.

Under the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to purchase humanitarian goods for its people suffering from sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait. The programme went into effect on Dec. 10 but no food or medicine has arrived in Iraq yet.
"The cabinet stressed Iraq would not tolerate the converation of its cause to fragmented branches for the American administration to gamble with," the radio said.

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan has said last week that the first shipments would arrive at the weekend, but the Undersecretary-General Yasushi Akashi later said he expected the first food and medical supplies to reach Iraq in mid-March.

Akashi said some countries on the Security Council did not want distribution to begin until the main complement of U.N. monitors who are to supervise the distribution were on the ground, which would occur about March 15.
